messages:
aman: FYI customer BrightHealth in eu-west-1 is blocked by their firewall — only whitelisted a few IPs and seeing timeouts / 403s to our hosted API. can we get a concise allowlist and proxy guidance they can hand to security?

sam_irvin: short answer: yes. we publish per-region egress CIDRs + a few fixed healthcheck IPs. pasting the current eu-west-1 set we gave SOC earlier (note: these are the runtime egress pools + model download pool).

sam_irvin: eu-west-1 egress CIDRs (current snapshot):
- 18.210.50.0/24
- 18.210.51.0/25
- 18.212.200.0/24
model-storage (downloads):
- 52.174.10.0/24
healthcheck sources:
- 18.210.60.10
- 18.210.60.11

leah_ux: do we need customers to open DNS/ntp ports too? its common for strict firewalls to block port 53 and outbound ntp.

nora_ops: yes — minimal ports to allow outbound from their app/cluster to our endpoints: 443 (TLS) always; 80 if they do non-TLS redirects; 53 udp/tcp to their recursive DNS (or to public resolvers if they rely on them); 123 udp for NTP if their infra blocks it. also recommend allowing outbound to our model-storage CIDR for large downloads.

nora_ops: proxy notes: if their outbound proxy requires auth, our SDKs and curl use HTTP CONNECT for TLS. the proxy must allow CONNECT to destination port 443 and must not terminate/rewrite the CONNECT Host header. TLS-inspecting proxies will break certificate pinning and SNI-based routing — for production we advise either passthrough or whitelisting the api hostnames for no-inspect.

leah_ux: they asked whether the healthchecks come from static ips (some vendors require single addr). can we confirm?

sam_irvin: healthchecks above (18.210.60.10/11) are stable for now — those are the LB source IPs for eu-west-1 control plane checks. runtime egress pools can change when we scale, so if they need a single static IP we should propose Dedicated or Private (both offer static NAT egress).

aman: they also worried about SNAT port exhaustion when we route many short-lived connections through a small NAT. any mitigations we can recommend?

nora_ops: common customer mitigations: increase ephemeral port range on their NAT gateway, enable port preservation (if supported), or use pooling (per-pod NAT pools) to avoid single-IP exhaustion. also use HTTP/2 or keepalive so connections are reused instead of new TCP handshakes for each request.

sam_irvin: sample firewall ACLs they can paste: 
iptables rules (example):
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 18.210.50.0/24 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 18.212.200.0/24 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# allow DNS to their recursive resolver (replace with your resolver IP)
iptables -A OUTPUT -p udp -d 10.0.0.2 --dport 53 -j ACCEPT

# sample curl via auth proxy (to validate CONNECT)
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp.local:8080
curl -v -x $HTTPS_PROXY https://api.redwood-inference.eu-west-1.example.com/v1/health

leah_ux: also callout: if their proxy does header stripping we need the X-Request-Id preserved for tracing.

aman: can we add a short blurb they can forward to security & infra teams summarizing tradeoffs and ask them to confirm whether they allow DNS to public resolvers or only internal resolvers?

sam_irvin: done — paste this into an email to SOC: 
"Please allow outbound TCP/UDP to the following CIDRs for EU-WEST-1 to enable Redwood hosted inference: 18.210.50.0/24, 18.210.51.0/25, 18.212.200.0/24, and 52.174.10.0/24 (model storage). Allow inbound healthcheck probes from 18.210.60.10 and 18.210.60.11. Permit HTTPS (443) to these ranges. If you use an outbound proxy, ensure CONNECT to port 443 is allowed and TLS is not terminated for api.redwood-inference.* hostnames. If a static egress IP is required, consider our Dedicated/Private options which provide static NAT egress."

nora_ops: final note: we rotate the runtime pools occasionally — we publish a canonical list on https://status.redwood-inference.com/egress-ips and post updates in #eng-platform when we change them. for strict firewalls recommend either: 1) allow hostname-based egress (DNS + TLS passthrough), or 2) accept a CIDR allowlist and plan for the rare update window.

egress-bot: NOTICE: eu-west-1 egress pool scheduled rotation on 1768080000 — customers on strict allowlists notified. :bell:

aman: great — I'll send this to the BrightHealth SOC and follow up if they push back on dynamic CIDRs. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
